t: A policy is issued for the dwelling of a house owner for 5 years under Method B of the long-term dwelling rules. The premium chargeable is
o: 5 years' premium with 10% automatic increase in SI each year
5 years' premium in advance less 15% discount
5 years' premium in advance less 25% discount
e: Long-term dwelling policies (min 3 years): Method A – full premium with SI deemed increased 10% each year; Method B – discounts of 15% (3 yrs), 20% (4), 25% (5), 30% (6), 35% (7), 40% (8), 45% (9), 50% (10+).

t: An SFSP policy for 7 months on a sum insured of ₹1 crore at ₹1.50‰ annual rate carries a premium of
e: Annual premium = 1,00,00,000 × 1.5/1000 = ₹15,000; for a period not exceeding 7 months the scale is 75% = ₹11,250.

t: A dwelling long-term policy of 5 years is sought to be cancelled in the second year. Refund of premium is
o: Allowed pro-rata for the unexpired years
Not allowed for mid-term cancellation of long-term dwelling policies
Allowed at 50% of the unexpired premium
e: Section III Rule 7: no refund for mid-term cancellation of long-term dwelling policies; mid-term inclusion of perils is also not allowed; mid-term increase in SI is pro-rata.

t: Under SFSP, loss or damage due to earthquake is
o: A general exclusion, insurable as an add-on cover
e: EQ, volcanic eruption and other convulsions of nature are excluded; the Earthquake (Fire and Shock) add-on covers them, with a 72-hour single-event clause.

t: An SFSP policy with sum insured ₹3,000 crore at a location suffers a loss of ₹8 crore. The minimum deductible is
e: SI above ₹2,500 crore per location: 5% of the claim subject to a minimum of ₹50 lakh; 5% of ₹8 crore = ₹40 lakh, so the minimum of ₹50 lakh applies.

t: Which of the following is excluded under SFSP unless expressly stated in the policy?
o: Goods held in trust or on commission
e: Items such as goods held in trust, bullion, curios over ₹10,000, documents, cheques, books of accounts and computer records need to be expressly included.

t: Condition 1 of the SFSP policy makes the policy voidable in the event of
o: Misrepresentation, mis-description or non-disclosure of any material particular
e: Condition 1: voidable for misrepresentation, mis-description or non-disclosure; Condition 3 deals with alteration of risk.

t: The condition of average (Condition 10) applies
o: To the total sum insured as a whole
Separately to each item of the policy where there are several items
e: Condition 10: if property is of greater value than the SI the insured bears a rateable proportion; every item, if more than one, is separately subject to the condition.

t: Within how many days of a loss must the insured deliver a written claim with particulars under Condition 6 of the SFSP policy?
e: ★ Key fact (repeated across the mocks of this paper). Condition 6(i): notice of loss forthwith, and within 15 days (or such further time as the insurer allows in writing) a written claim with particulars and details of other insurances.

t: A property is insured against fire for ₹30,000 while its value at risk is ₹40,000. A fire causes a loss of ₹16,000. The insurer pays
e: Average: loss × SI/VAR = 16,000 × 30,000/40,000 = ₹12,000; the insured bears ₹4,000 as his own insurer.

t: The Start-up Expenses add-on covers
o: Start-up costs necessarily and reasonably incurred consequent upon a loss covered by the policy
Expenses of setting up a new business
e: Start-up expenses extension (policy rate on specified SI) pays start-up costs following an insured loss; BSUS provides ₹1 lakh and BLUS ₹5 lakh inbuilt.

t: Spontaneous combustion add-on for Category III goods is rated at
o: ₹0.75‰ on the sum insured of the relative commodity
e: Spontaneous combustion rates: Category I ₹0.25‰, II ₹0.50‰, III ₹0.75‰, IV ₹1.00‰ on the SI of the commodity; goods are classified into four categories for this cover.

t: Once add-on covers have been included mid-term, cancellation of the add-on alone mid-term
o: Attracts no refund unless the policy is cancelled or replaced simultaneously
e: Note 1 to Section VIII: mid-term inclusion of add-ons is charged annual premium; no refund on cancelling an add-on mid-term unless the policy is cancelled or replaced by a fresh policy with the add-ons.

t: Stock of ₹2.5 lakh is covered by an SFSP policy for ₹1 lakh and a declaration policy for ₹2 lakh. Loss ₹1 lakh. The declaration policy pays
e: Excess of stock value over SFSP SI = 2.5 − 1 = ₹1.5 lakh, which is less than the declaration SI, so the excess is used: 1,00,000 × 1.5/2.5 = ₹60,000; SFSP pays 1,00,000 × 1/2.5 = ₹40,000; total ₹1 lakh.

t: Under a declaration policy, monthly declarations may be based on
o: Book value at cost on any day
The closing stock on the last day of the month only
The average of values at risk on each day of the month or the highest value at risk during the month
The opening stock of the month only
e: AIFT Rule 14(b): two modes – average of daily values at risk or highest value during the month; declaration due by the last day of the succeeding month.

t: Under the Agreed Bank Clause, when a claim is paid to the bank and the insurer contends that no liability existed as regards the mortgagor,
o: The insurer is subrogated to the bank's rights to the extent of the payment
The policy is cancelled ab initio
The bank must refund the claim
The mortgagor must repay the insurer with interest
e: Clause (vi): on paying the bank where no liability existed towards the owner, the insurer becomes legally subrogated to the rights of the bank to that extent.

t: Detached blocks of a risk protected by an automatic sprinkler installation with independent pumping arrangements are allowed a reduction on the basic rate of
e: Sprinklered blocks get a 5% reduction on the basic rate (step 2 of the rate computation) in Sections III, IV, V and VI; this is separate from the FEA discount.

t: An insured opts for a voluntary deductible of ₹20 lakh (AOG) / ₹10 lakh (other perils). The discount on the final premium is
e: Voluntary deductible table: ₹10 lakh/₹5 lakh – 2%; ₹20 lakh/₹10 lakh – 4%; ₹30/15 lakh – 6%; ₹60/30 lakh – 8%; ₹100/50 lakh – 10%; higher – refer TAC. The voluntary deductible is in addition to the compulsory excess.

t: Under Bharat Griha Raksha, theft is covered
o: Only if the burglary add-on is taken
Within 7 days following the operation of any of the insured perils
At all times during the policy period
Within 30 days of any insured peril
e: BGR, BSUS and BLUS have inbuilt cover for theft within 7 days following an insured peril; SFSP does not cover theft.

t: The discount for stand-by machinery under MBD is 50%, except in the case of
e: ★ Key fact (repeated across the mocks of this paper). Stand-by discount of 50% is allowed except for DG sets; standstill discount up to 50% (minimum 3 months); spares such as rotors/windings get 50%.

t: The policy to be offered to a shop with total value at risk of ₹3 crore (building, stock and furniture) is
e: BSUS covers non-dwelling risks (offices, hotels, shops, industrial, storage, tank farms) where total value at risk does not exceed ₹5 crore at one location.

t: In the storage classification of goods, which material falls in Category 3?
o: Flammable liquids with flash point above 65°C
Explosives such as TNT and ammonium nitrate
e: Category 3: explosives, self-ignitable materials, liquids with flash point below 32°C, strong oxidising agents, combustible gases and waste of Category 2 and 3 materials.

t: Which of the following is 'excluded property' under an IAR policy unless specifically covered?
o: Plant and machinery in the factory
Vehicles licensed for road use and property in transit outside the premises
e: IAR excluded property: money/documents, goods in trust, road vehicles/aircraft/watercraft, property in transit, property under construction, land/roads/dams/pipelines, livestock/crops, property undergoing process, property more specifically insured, property removed (except machinery for repair up to 60 days).

t: A business has departments A, B and C with turnovers 100, 100 and 50 before loss. After a fire in A, turnovers are 50, 125 and 75 (total unchanged). With the Departmental Clause, the loss of turnover for the claim is
o: Nil, since total turnover is unchanged
100, the full turnover of department A
50, since the results of each department affected are considered separately
25, the net of increases and decreases
e: Departmental clause: the reduction in turnover and ICW provisions apply separately to each affected department; without the clause the claim would be nil as total turnover was maintained.

t: For a 250 MW combined-cycle gas-based power plant under EAR, the minimum deductible for a testing-period claim is
o: 10% of the claim subject to a minimum of ₹50 lakh
5% of the claim subject to a minimum of ₹60 lakh
5% of the claim subject to a minimum of ₹125 lakh
5% of the claim subject to a minimum of ₹100 lakh
e: ★ Key fact (repeated across the mocks of this paper). Combined-cycle/gas plants: 50–200 MW – min ₹60 lakh testing/₹20 lakh normal; 200–300 MW – ₹100 lakh/₹50 lakh; 300 MW and above – ₹125 lakh/₹75 lakh.

t: Which of the following Acts is specifically relevant to insurance of mining machinery?
e: Specific statutes for engineering insurance: Factories Act 1948, Indian Boilers Act 1923 and Mines Act 1952.

t: Which of the following is NOT underwritten as an engineering class of business?
e: IAR is a fire-department package (fire MD + MBD + FLOP/MLOP); CAR, EAR, CPM, MBD, EEI, BPP, DOS and MLOP are engineering covers.

t: Which of the following is a covered peril under EAR/SCE?
o: Loss discovered at the time of inventory
Damage caused by negligence of the contractor's employees
Loss or damage due to faulty design
Cost of rectifying an erection error without physical damage
e: Human risks – carelessness, strike, riot and faults in erection – are covered; inventory losses, faulty design (subject to DE wording) and pure rectification costs are excluded.

t: An EAR proposal is received on 15 May, but the first consignment reached site on 1 May. The premium rate is charged
o: From the date of beginning of erection
From the date of payment of premium
From the date the proposal was received
For the total project period commencing from the date of arrival of the first consignment
e: Rating is for the entire project period from arrival of the first consignment/commencement of work; the insurer is not liable for damage that occurred before the commencement of insurance.

t: To claim refund for early completion under an EAR policy, the minimum period of early completion is
e: Refund conditions: period of insurance more than 18 months, claims below 60%, and minimum 3 months for which refund is claimed, after reworking premium on the reduced period.

t: Under EAR, cessation of work (whether total or partial) is
o: Covered subject to a 7-day time excess
e: General exclusions of EAR/CAR: war, nuclear reaction, wilful negligence and cessation of work; material damage exclusions include excess, inventory losses, wear and tear, faulty design and packing material.

t: For an EAR policy with SI ₹30 crore at an unprotected site, the excess for a fire claim is
o: 20% of the claim with an upper limit of ₹3 crore
10% of the claim with an upper limit of ₹5 crore
10% of the claim subject to a minimum of the testing period excess, with an upper limit of ₹2 crore
e: Fire at unprotected sites with SI below ₹50 crore: 10% of claim, minimum testing excess, cap ₹2 crore; above ₹50 crore: 20%, cap ₹3 crore.

t: Under EAR/SCE/CAR the Third Party Liability extension does NOT cover
o: Legal liability for accidental damage to property of other persons
Costs and expenses of litigation recovered by a claimant
Legal liability for damage to property held in trust or in the custody of the insured
Costs incurred with the insurer's written consent
e: TPL covers liability to third parties and litigation costs but excludes property held in trust/custody of the insured, property used in connection with the erection, employees' injuries and road vehicles.

t: The obligatory cession that Indian general insurers must make to GIC Re is currently:
e: ★ Core fact (asked across III papers). The obligatory cession was reduced to 4% from 1 April 2022.

t: Discount on terrorism premium under project policies is allowed where the policy period
o: Is any period, as terrorism is a flat rate
e: Per the question bank, discount on terrorism premium is allowed for project policy periods exceeding 12 months; the Terrorism Pool is managed by GIC.

t: Catalyst included in the EAR sum insured is
o: Covered only under the marine policy
Automatically covered for storage and erection risks at the normal rate, and covered during hot testing on payment of additional premium
Covered during hot testing without additional premium
e: Catalyst is covered for storage/erection when its value is in the SI; hot-testing cover for catalyst requires additional premium.

t: An 18-month EAR policy with total premium ₹10 lakh is to be paid in instalments. The number of instalments and the first instalment amount are
A defective part (A) damages the machine it is fitted in (B), a connected machine (C) and surrounding property (D). Under DE4 cover, what is payable?
e: DE4 excludes only the defective component and access costs; the machine containing it (B), connected machine (C) and surrounding property (D) are payable.

t: For covering the marine portion under an MCE policy, the underwriter needs
o: Sum insured for both overseas and inland transit
Sum insured for inland transit only
e: MCE needs marine values for overseas and inland transit in addition to project information such as nature, duration, testing period, TPL limit and additional customs duty.

t: Which of the following is a covered cause of loss under MBD?
e: MBD covers short circuit, entry of foreign bodies, negligence, lubrication failure, insulation failure and metallurgical failure; fire and allied perils (including flood and lightning) and boiler explosions are excluded.

t: Mid-term increase of sum insured under MBD/EEI/BPP/CPM policies is charged
o: On the short-period scale for the unexpired period
Free, if the increase is below 10%
e: Operational engineering policies: increase/decrease of SI is on short-period scale; if the policy is renewed with the same insurer at the enhanced SI, the difference between short-period and pro-rata premium is refunded.

t: In a total loss claim under MBD, the amount payable is
o: Actual value of the item immediately before the loss, including freight, erection and customs duty if included in the SI, less salvage
Repair cost of an equivalent machine
e: Total loss: actual (depreciated) value immediately before the loss plus normal dismantling charges; extra charges for overtime, holidays and express freight are payable only if specifically covered.

t: Which of the following statements about EEI is correct?
o: It covers neither breakdown nor voltage fluctuation
It covers breakdown but not voltage fluctuation
It covers electrical or mechanical breakdown of the insured item and damage caused by voltage fluctuation
It covers voltage fluctuation but not breakdown
e: EEI Section I is an all-risks cover including breakdown, short circuit and over-voltage along with fire, EQ, flood, theft and impact.

t: Under the BPP policy, the standstill discount available is
o: Up to 50% based on the standstill period, minimum 3 months
Up to 25% for any idle period
Up to 75% for a minimum of 6 months
e: BPP: SI on CNRV, annual or short period, escalation can be opted, standstill discount up to 50% (minimum 3 months), excess ₹10,000 per the notes.

t: How many classified groups of machinery exist under the CPM tariff?
e: CPM machinery is classified into five groups; the deductible circular prescribes a value-band excess for Groups I–IV (including cranes above 10 tonnes under Group III) and ₹2,500 flat for Group V.

t: The principle that allows an insurer who has paid a claim to step into the insured's shoes and recover from a liable third party is:
e: ★ Core fact (asked across III papers). Subrogation is a corollary of indemnity; it does not apply to life or personal accident (benefit) policies.

t: The minimum policy period for a Deterioration of Stocks policy is
e: DOS minimum period is 7 months; declaration policies require 12 months, stock above ₹50 lakh and fortnightly declarations.

t: Loss of Profit following a boiler explosion is covered under
o: Boiler/Pressure Plant Loss of Profit (BPPLOP), on the lines of MLOP
e: MLOP and BPPLOP cover BI losses consequent on material damage under the respective MB/BPP policies: net profit, insured standing charges and ICW.

t: For CPM equipment of individual value up to ₹1 lakh, the minimum deductible for an AOG claim is
o: 5% of the sum insured subject to a minimum of ₹10,000
10% of the sum insured subject to a minimum of ₹5,000
2% of the sum insured subject to a minimum of ₹1,500
e: CPM table: up to ₹1 lakh – AOG 10% of SI min ₹5,000, other perils 2% min ₹1,500; ₹1–5 lakh – 5% min ₹10,000 / 1.5% min ₹2,000.

t: For a CAR policy covering an irrigation canal project with SI ₹800 crore, the deductibles in the TAC tariff are increased to
o: 15 times the minimum amount, as it is a specialised risk
e: Specialised risks – all works in water, dams, canals, hydro projects, tunnels, irrigation systems and caverns – carry 15 times the TAC minimum deductibles irrespective of SI, with ALOP time excess 45 days (max 75).
